source_text: Quibus gestis inter voluminis primas partes, progressus est ad distinctionem nuptiarum et concupiscentiae, sicut fuerat tituli inscriptione pollicitus; deditque toto deinceps opere documentum artis et virtutis suae. Inter negationem enim confessorum et negatorum confessionem ultima necessitate vexatus, quid aerumnarum pateretur foeda conscientia publicavit.
pass_a_gloss: Which things having been done among the first parts of the volume, he advanced to the distinction of marriages and of concupiscence, as he had promised by the inscription of the title; and through the whole work thereafter he gave a proof of his art and virtue. For, harassed by last necessity between denial of things confessed and confession of things denied, he published what distresses a foul conscience was suffering.

lemmas.lexica: LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good
LS necessitas; Blaise vs free choice

pass_b_english: After doing this in the opening parts of the volume, he proceeded to distinguish marriage from sexual desire, as the wording of his title had promised. Throughout the rest of the work he then displayed his skill and virtue. Driven to the last extremity between denying what he had admitted and admitting what he had denied, he publicly exposed the torments of his foul conscience.

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
